question: A man sold an article at a gain of 57%. If he had sold it for ₹238 more, he would have gained 82%. The cost price (in ₹) of the article is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Difference in **Gain%** = 82% − 57% = 25%.

This **25% difference** is equivalent to the extra amount of **₹238**.

Using **unitary method**: 25% of CP = 238.

Therefore, 100% of CP = 238 × 4 = **952**.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹952.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial Profit = 57%, Final Profit = 82%, Increase in SP = ₹238.

**Formulas:** SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100 | Profit = SP − CP

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/59ab1cfdab4106171dd0997f63ab707566179612f0a38828243b780df7a466e1.png] 

⇒ Let the **Cost Price (CP)** be x.

⇒ First Selling Price (SP₁) = 1.57x.

⇒ Second Selling Price (SP₂) = 1.82x.

⇒ According to the question: SP₂ − SP₁ = 238.

⇒ 1.82x − 1.57x = 238 ⇒ 0.25x = 238.

⇒ x = 238 ÷ 0.25 = 238 × 4 = 952.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹952.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss on Cost Price

Unless stated otherwise, **Profit%** or **Loss%** is always calculated on the **Cost Price (CP)**. Formula: Profit% = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

Relation between Gain and SP

If there are two different gain percentages g₁ and g₂ on the same CP, the difference in SP is equal to the **difference in gain percentages** of the CP.
